Hi Jonas —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Please find attached our redlined order form (BrightPath_OrderForm_v3_redlines.pdf). There are three items we need clarified from Redwood before we can route to procurement:

1) Output title vs. license: the customer is pushing for explicit assignment of "output title" for specific deliverables used in their end-product. Our legal prefers a non-exclusive license. Can Redwood confirm whether assignment is feasible for named deliverables only?

2) Training / feedback license: we want a firm opt-out for training on customer-provided prompts/data; currently the doc leaves feedback rights broad.

3) Telemetry/evidence handoff: procurement needs a concrete evidence manifest (sample outputs + telemetry) and an access mechanism (S3 or shared drive) with retention windows. Who on your side owns that handoff?

We're aiming to finalize commercial terms this month. If it's helpful, Elena (cc'd) can coordinate procurement timelines.

Attachments: BrightPath_OrderForm_v3_redlines.pdf (PDF, 480KB)

Thanks,
Sasha Kim
Head of Legal & Partnerships

If you require ongoing log access we can provide a scoped S3-share with strict IAM controls for the duration agreed in the SOW.

Next steps:

- Laura (ops) can confirm S3 bucket provisioning and the handoff runbook.
- Sasha/Elena: can you confirm whether assignment is limited to a named list of artifacts (yes/no) and whether procurement needs a continuous log stream or a one-time package?

Subject: Re: Draft order form (v3) — output title, training opt-out & evidence handoff

Jonas / Sasha —

Quick legal perspective and draft clause language to keep momentum. I reviewed the brightpath redlines and Jon's notes. High level: assignment for a narrow list of deliverables is workable; full assignment of all runtime outputs is a no-go for us. Below are suggested additions to the MSA/Order Form. Please treat these as internal drafts until countersigned.

Suggested additions (deliverable-level assignment + opt-out attestation):
- "Assigned Deliverables": Customer may list specific artifacts in Exhibit A. Redwood will assign title to those artifacts upon payment of the applicable milestone fee. Assignment is limited to listed artifacts and does not include underlying model weights, prompts, or system logs.

- "Output License": Except for Assigned Deliverables, Customer is granted a perpetual, worldwide, non-exclusive, transferable license to use, reproduce, modify, and distribute outputs produced by the Services.

- "Training Exclusion & Attestation": Customer may elect an opt-out for training in the Order Form. Redwood will exclude opt-out-designated data from its training pipelines and provide a quarterly attestation describing the exclusion process and scope. Customer will have the right to request a one-time, redacted verification sample (no raw training data).

- "Telemetry & Evidence Handoff": At contract effective date, Redwood will provide a packaged evidence manifest containing sample outputs, redaction summary, and a telemetry CSV (fields: request_id, timestamp, route, token_count, error_code). By default Redwood retains telemetry for 90 days; extended retention available by mutual agreement. Access mechanism: scoped S3 bucket with time-limited credentials; cross-account role can be configured if BrightPath provides account ID.

Operational asks for next week:
1) Laura: confirm whether ops can automate generating the telemetry CSV and a signed S3 pre-signed URL (we'll include this in the SOW).
2) Jonas: capture which internal teams (security/compliance) we should include for the handoff checklist.
3) Sasha/Elena: confirm whether procurement requires an ongoing log stream or the one-time package + quarterly attestation. If ongoing, put that as a line-item in the SOW for pricing.

Attachment: legal_clause_suggestions.txt (plain text, 6KB)

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Contracts & IP
Redwood Inference
